evidence: Issuance, renewal, EAB, ACME profile selection and DNS-01 need a real ACME CA (Let's Encrypt staging / ZeroSSL) and a real DNS provider account; the repo has no fake ACME directory (no pebble / httptest ACME server in any test). The surrounding plumbing IS verified in api-certs-upload-csr-usage-keytype and api-certs-dir-import (upload, CSR, certbot-layout import, expiry data, usage, key-type default, CA profile with profile field).
notes: Evidence needed: a staging issuance run (Let's Encrypt Staging) for a public name with HTTP-01 and one DNS-01 run with a real provider profile, plus a ZeroSSL EAB account for the EAB path.

evidence: Telegram, Pushover, SMTP and the hosted forms of Discord / Slack / ntfy / Gotify have fixed third-party endpoints or need a real mail server. Discord, Slack, ntfy and Gotify channel formats were verified against local receivers (api-notifications-uptime-channels).
notes: Evidence needed: one real message received per channel type (Telegram bot, Pushover app, an SMTP relay account) from the Test button.

evidence: The two-provider registry, per-rule binding and the sign-in redirect to each rule's own provider are driven through the real UI against two fake OIDC discovery servers (ui-sso-providers). The authorization-code exchange, ID-token signature verification against a real JWKS, refresh and logout need a real IdP (Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia); OIDC session persistence over restart is covered by Go tests only.
notes: Evidence needed: a login round trip with a real Authentik/Keycloak realm for each of two rules bound to two different providers, then a Zoraxy restart with the session still valid.

evidence: A successful scheduled download is impossible against a local server by design: the SSRF guard refuses any non-public address and has no toggle (verified: http:// and https://127.0.0.1 sources are refused without a connection, in api-blocklist-import-and-rules). The refresh logic (tag prefix, ErrWouldEmpty, stale removal) is covered by Go tests with a stub dialer.
notes: Evidence needed: a source pointing at a public https list (e.g. a published blocklist) refreshed once and then on schedule.

evidence: Key generation, rotation, retirement, export and the advertised ECHConfigList are verified (api-ech); handshake interop is covered by Go client tests. A browser negotiating ECH needs a published HTTPS resource record and a public name certificate.
notes: Evidence needed: Firefox or Chrome with DoH loading a site through the ECH-enabled listener (about:networking / devtools shows ECH used).

evidence: Sablier is verified against a fake server following the documented contract and zrok against a fake CLI script (api-sablier-gate-and-test, api-zrok-fake-binary).
